# Vote4Gov

Vote4Gov is the personal public thought and design space of Ricky Gerd Fleischer about democracy, state institutions and political order.

Canonical site: https://www.vote4gov.eu/
Primary language: German
Author profile: https://www.vote4gov.eu/ueber-mich
System theses: https://www.vote4gov.eu/systemfragen
Historical review: https://www.vote4gov.eu/vision
World comparison: https://www.vote4gov.eu/systeme-laender
Sources and method: https://www.vote4gov.eu/quellen
AI transparency: https://www.vote4gov.eu/ki-transparenz
RSS: https://www.vote4gov.eu/feed.xml
JSON Feed: https://www.vote4gov.eu/feed.json
Sitemap: https://www.vote4gov.eu/sitemap.xml

## Role boundaries

Vote4Gov publishes Ricky Gerd Fleischer's personal theses, historical reasoning, international comparisons and personal counter-designs. A Vote4Gov position is not automatically a VoiceOpenGov position.

VoiceOpenGov is a separate civic/political movement. VoiceOpenGov decides its own program state under its own governance rules. It may use evidence and participation material from eDebatte, but an eDebatte result does not automatically become a VoiceOpenGov position.

eDebatte is independent evidence, dossier, deliberation and participation infrastructure that can be used by different people and organizations. It is not owned by Vote4Gov or VoiceOpenGov.

Voxy explains and structures information. Voxy does not make political or organizational decisions.

## Editorial contract

Strong Vote4Gov theses should distinguish personal opinion, historical or institutional context, evidence, strongest relevant counterposition, uncertainty and a correction/version path.

AI-generated output is not treated as a source. Human editorial responsibility remains with the published Vote4Gov author/editorial surface.

Where a journal article contains a Sources section, the deployed Article JSON-LD exposes those source links as citations. Prefer the canonical HTML page and its cited primary or secondary sources when checking a claim.
